records.source: וַיְצַ֤ו מֹשֶׁה֙ וְזִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁמֹר֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And commanded Moses and [the] elders of Israel the people, saying, keep all the commandment which I [am] commanding you today.
pieces: Moses and the elders of Israel gave the people this command: "Keep the whole commandment that I am giving you today.

L.1: And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, "Keep all the commandment that I am commanding you today.

R.1: Moses and the elders of Israel gave orders to the people. They said, "Obey all the commands I am giving you today.

decisions.choice: Moses speaks, with the elders standing beside him
alternatives: Moses and the elders speak together as one voice
decisions.reason: The verb "commanded" is singular and the speaker says "I", so Moses is the one speaking. The elders join him because they will lead the people after his death and see that these orders are carried out in the land (31:9, 28).

decisions.choice: all the commandment: the whole of what Moses commands, taken as one
decisions.reason: The word is singular, as in 5:31, 6:1 and 8:1. It names the whole body of Moses' teaching as one charge to be kept, not one single rule.

decisions.choice: the elders: the heads of families and clans who led the tribes
decisions.reason: Elders were the older men who spoke for their families and tribes and settled matters in the towns (19:12; 21:19; 22:15). Here they stand with Moses as witnesses and future guardians of the covenant.

decisions.choice: the whole commandment (Balanced); all the commands (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the singular as "the whole commandment" to show it is one charge. Readable uses the plural, which plain English expects for a set of rules; the sense is the same.

records.heading: Stones and an altar on Mount Ebal

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה בַּיּוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעַבְר֣וּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ אֶל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֣ן לָ֑ךְ וַהֲקֵמֹתָ֤ לְךָ֙ אֲבָנִ֣ים גְּדֹל֔וֹת וְשַׂדְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֖ם בַּשִּֽׂיד׃
records.gloss: And it will be, on the day which you cross the Jordan into the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you, and you will set up for yourself great stones and you will plaster them with plaster.
pieces: On the day you cross the Jordan into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you, set up some large stones and coat them with plaster.

L.2: And it shall be, on the day that you cross the Jordan into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you, that you shall set up for yourself large stones and coat them with plaster.

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you a land across the Jordan River. When you cross over into it, set up some large stones and cover them with plaster.

decisions.choice: on the day that: at the time when, not necessarily the very same day
decisions.reason: "On the day" often means "when" (Genesis 2:4). Mount Ebal lies well inside the land, some days' journey from the river crossing, and Joshua carries out this command after the first battles in the land (Joshua 8:30-35). Verse 4 says simply "when you have crossed the Jordan".

decisions.choice: coat them with plaster: a smooth surface of lime to write on
decisions.reason: The stones were covered with lime plaster so the words could be written on them clearly (verses 3, 8). Writing in ink on plastered walls is known from the region in this period; a text written on plaster was found at Deir Alla, east of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: you cross ... you set up: Israel addressed as many and as one
decisions.reason: "You cross" is plural and "you set up" is singular. As often in Deuteronomy, the people are spoken to both as many members and as one nation (11:26).

decisions.choice: states the gift of the land first, then the command
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long Hebrew sentence into two short ones and adds "River" to make clear what the Jordan is.

records.source: וְכָתַבְתָּ֣ עֲלֵיהֶ֗ן אֶֽת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֛י הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בְּעָבְרֶ֑ךָ לְמַ֡עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ תָּבֹ֨א אֶל־הָאָ֜רֶץ אֲֽשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֣יךָ׀נֹתֵ֣ן לְךָ֗ אֶ֣רֶץ זָבַ֤ת חָלָב֙ וּדְבַ֔שׁ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־אֲבֹתֶ֖יךָ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And you will write on them all [the] words of the law the this, when you cross over, so that you may come into the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you, a land flowing [with] milk and honey, as spoke Yahweh [the] God of your fathers to you.
pieces: When you have crossed over, write on them every word of this law, so that you may enter the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, promised you.

L.3: And you shall write on them all the words of this law, when you have crossed over, so that you may go into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, spoke to you.

R.3: After you cross over, write on the stones every word of this teaching. Then you will go into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you. It is a land rich with milk and honey. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, promised you.

decisions.choice: all the words of this law: the teaching Moses has given, how much is not said
decisions.reason: "This law" is Moses' teaching in this book (1:5; 17:18). The stones could hold the commands of chapters 12-26, a shorter core of them, or more; the text does not say. Joshua 8:32 says Joshua wrote on the stones "a copy of the law of Moses".

decisions.choice: so that you may go into the land: the writing goes with the entry into the land
decisions.reason: The words "so that" tie the writing of the law to Israel's entry and life in the land: the land is entered and held under this law. They can also be read more loosely, "when you cross over to enter the land".

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: a land of rich pasture and plenty
decisions.reason: Milk from flocks and herds and honey (from bees, or the syrup of dates and figs) picture a fertile, generous land, as in 6:3 and 11:9 and Exodus 3:8.

decisions.choice: promised you
decisions.reason: The verb is "spoke". Balanced and Readable say "promised", since what the LORD spoke to the fathers was the promise of the land (1:8; 6:3). Literal keeps "spoke".

decisions.choice: this teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for the Hebrew word usually rendered "law" here, as in 1:5 and 17:18: it is all that Moses teaches, not only rules.

records.source: וְהָיָה֮ בְּעָבְרְכֶ֣ם אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ תָּקִ֜ימוּ אֶת־הָאֲבָנִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֜י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֛ם הַיּ֖וֹם בְּהַ֣ר עֵיבָ֑ל וְשַׂדְתָּ֥ אוֹתָ֖ם בַּשִּֽׂיד׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when you cross the Jordan, you will set up the stones the these, which I [am] commanding you today, on Mount Ebal, and you will plaster them with plaster.
pieces: When you have crossed the Jordan, put these stones up on Mount Ebal and coat them with plaster, as I command you today.

L.4: And it shall be, when you have crossed the Jordan, you shall set up these stones, as I am commanding you today, on Mount Ebal, and you shall coat them with plaster.

R.4: After you cross the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I am telling you today. Cover them with plaster.

decisions.choice: on Mount Ebal
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "Ebal". The Samaritan Pentateuch reads "Gerizim", the mountain of the blessing and the Samaritans' holy mountain, and one Old Latin witness agrees with it. Joshua 8:30 follows the Hebrew: Joshua built the altar on Mount Ebal.

decisions.choice: as I am commanding you: the stones of verse 2, in the way just described
decisions.reason: The word normally means "which"; here it points back to the command already given in verses 2-3.

decisions.choice: Mount Ebal: the northern of the two mountains at Shechem
decisions.reason: Ebal and Gerizim face each other across the valley of Shechem (11:29-30). Ebal is named as the mountain for the curse (verse 13), and it is there that the law is written and the altar built.

records.source: וּבָנִ֤יתָ שָּׁם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ מִזְבַּ֣ח אֲבָנִ֔ים לֹא־תָנִ֥יף עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם בַּרְזֶֽל׃
records.gloss: And you will build there an altar to Yahweh your God, an altar of stones; not you will wield on them iron.
pieces: Build an altar there to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, an altar of stones. Do not use any iron tool on them.

L.5: And you shall build there an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, an altar of stones; you shall not wield iron on them.

R.5: Build an altar there for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Make it out of stones, and do not use iron tools to cut them.

decisions.choice: no iron on the stones: the altar law of Exodus 20
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:22 (Hebrew numbering) commands an altar of earth or of uncut stone, "for if you wield your tool on it, you have profaned it". The altar is to be made from what God made, not shaped by human craft.

decisions.choice: wield iron: swing an iron tool, such as a chisel
decisions.reason: The verb means to swing or wave something; with "iron" it means to cut or dress the stones with an iron tool.

decisions.choice: iron tool
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "tool", since "iron" here stands for an iron cutting tool.

records.source: אֲבָנִ֤ים שְׁלֵמוֹת֙ תִּבְנֶ֔ה אֶת־מִזְבַּ֖ח יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְהַעֲלִ֤יתָ עָלָיו֙ עוֹלֹ֔ת לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Stones whole you will build the altar of Yahweh your God, and you will offer up on it burnt offerings to Yahweh your God.
pieces: Use uncut stones to build the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and offer burnt offerings on it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.6: Of whole stones you shall build the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you shall offer burnt offerings on it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.6: Use stones from the field, just as they are, to build the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Then offer burnt offerings on it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: whole stones: stones left uncut, as they were found
decisions.reason: The word means complete or unharmed. Here it means stones not cut or shaped by tools (verse 5; compare 1 Kings 6:7).

decisions.choice: burnt offerings: animals burned whole on the altar
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was given entirely to God and burned completely (Leviticus 1). It expressed full devotion and was offered at the start of worship.

decisions.choice: stones from the field, just as they are
decisions.reason: Readable explains "uncut" in plain words.

records.source: וְזָבַחְתָּ֥ שְׁלָמִ֖ים וְאָכַ֣לְתָּ שָּׁ֑ם וְשָׂ֣מַחְתָּ֔ לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you will sacrifice peace offerings and you will eat there, and you will rejoice before Yahweh your God.
pieces: Sacrifice peace offerings, eat them there, and rejoice in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.7: And you shall sacrifice peace offerings and eat there, and you shall rejoice before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.7: Offer peace offerings and eat them there. Celebrate in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: peace offerings: sacrifices shared in a meal
decisions.reason: Part of a peace offering was burned for God, part went to the priest, and the rest was eaten by the worshipers (Leviticus 3; 7:11-21). It marked fellowship with God and with one another.

decisions.choice: eat and rejoice before the LORD: a covenant meal
decisions.reason: Eating and rejoicing in God's presence is the mark of worship in the land throughout Deuteronomy (12:7, 12; 16:11). At Sinai too, the covenant was sealed with a meal before God (Exodus 24:5, 11).

decisions.choice: eat them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is eaten: the meat of the peace offerings.

records.source: וְכָתַבְתָּ֣ עַל־הָאֲבָנִ֗ים אֶֽת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֛י הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בַּאֵ֥ר הֵיטֵֽב׃ס
records.gloss: And you will write on the stones all [the] words of the law the this, making [it] clear well.
pieces: And write on the stones all the words of this law, very clearly."

L.8: And you shall write on the stones all the words of this law, making [them] very plain."

R.8: Write every word of this teaching on the stones, so that it is very clear and easy to read."

decisions.choice: making them very plain: written clearly, easy to read
decisions.reason: The verb means to make clear. With writing it means to write legibly, as in Habakkuk 2:2, "make it plain on tablets". In 1:5 the same verb is used of Moses setting out the law clearly in speech.

decisions.choice: a repeat of verse 3: the command to write frames the passage
decisions.reason: Verses 2-3 and 4-8 each begin with setting up the stones and end with writing on them. The repetition closes the instructions given by Moses and the elders (verse 1).

decisions.choice: easy to read
decisions.reason: Readable adds "easy to read" to say what "very clear" means for writing.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים הַלְוִיִּ֔ם אֶ֥ל כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הַסְכֵּ֤ת׀וּשְׁמַע֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ נִהְיֵ֣יתָֽ לְעָ֔ם לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And spoke Moses and the priests the Levites to all Israel, saying, be silent and hear, Israel: the day the this you have become [a] people to Yahweh your God.
pieces: Then Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel: "Be still and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.9: And Moses and the priests, the Levites, spoke to all Israel, saying, "Be silent and hear, Israel: this day you have become a people for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.9: Then Moses and the priests from the tribe of Levi spoke to all the people of Israel. They said, "Be quiet and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people who belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: be silent: be still and pay attention
decisions.reason: This verb is found only here in the Hebrew Bible. Related words in neighboring languages mean to be quiet, so it calls for silent attention before the solemn words that follow.

decisions.choice: this day you have become the people of the LORD: the covenant is sealed today
decisions.reason: Israel was already the LORD's people (7:6; 14:2). What is new "this day" is the covenant made in Moab, in which Israel has declared that the LORD is its God and the LORD has declared Israel his own people (26:17-18; 29:11-12).

decisions.choice: the priests, the Levites: the priests, who belong to the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy calls the priests by their tribe (17:9; 18:1). They join Moses because they will keep the written law and read it to the people (31:9-11).

decisions.choice: the priests from the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: As in 17:18, Readable explains "Levitical priests".

records.heading: Today you have become the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: וְשָׁ֣מַעְתָּ֔ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ אֶת־מִצְוֺתָו֙וְאֶת־חֻקָּ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּֽוֹם׃ס
records.gloss: And you will listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God and you will do his commandments and his statutes which I [am] commanding you today.
pieces: So obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and carry out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and statutes that I am giving you today."

L.10: And you shall listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and do {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes that I am commanding you today."

R.10: So obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commands and follow {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws that I am giving you today."

decisions.choice: listen to the voice of: obey
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what they say (13:5; 15:5).

decisions.choice: and you shall listen: what follows from becoming his people
decisions.reason: The verb form looks forward and follows from verse 9: because Israel has become the LORD's people today, it is to obey him.

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable render the joining "and" as "So", to show that obeying follows from becoming God's people (verse 9).

decisions.choice: commandments and statutes (Literal, Balanced); commands and laws (Readable)
decisions.reason: These are the settled renderings for these two words in Deuteronomy.

records.source: וַיְצַ֤ו מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And commanded Moses the people on the day the that, saying,
pieces: On that day Moses gave the people this command:

L.11: And Moses commanded the people on that day, saying,

R.11: That same day Moses gave the people these orders:

decisions.choice: on that day: the day of the covenant in Moab
decisions.reason: "That day" is the day of verse 9, when Israel became the LORD's people. The orders that follow are for later, when the people have crossed into the land (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the narrator speaks; Moses' words begin in verse 12
decisions.reason: This verse is the narrator introducing a new speech of Moses. The speech that begins in verse 12 runs on through chapter 28, closing at 28:68.

records.heading: The curses from Mount Ebal

records.source: אֵ֠לֶּה יַֽעַמְד֞וּ לְבָרֵ֤ךְ אֶת־הָעָם֙ עַל־הַ֣ר גְּרִזִ֔ים בְּעָבְרְכֶ֖ם אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן שִׁמְעוֹן֙ וְלֵוִ֣י וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְיִשָּׂשכָ֖ר וְיוֹסֵ֥ף וּבִנְיָמִֽן׃
records.gloss: These will stand to bless the people on Mount Gerizim when you cross the Jordan: Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Joseph and Benjamin.
pieces: "When you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes are to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.

L.12: "These shall stand to bless the people on Mount Gerizim when you have crossed the Jordan: Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Joseph and Benjamin.

R.12: "After you cross the Jordan, these tribes must stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.

decisions.choice: the six tribes on Gerizim: all sons of Jacob's wives Leah and Rachel
decisions.reason: Simeon, Levi, Judah and Issachar are sons of Leah; Joseph and Benjamin are sons of Rachel (Genesis 35:23-24). Joseph stands for the two tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, so Levi can be counted among the twelve here.

decisions.choice: to bless the people: the words of the blessing are not given here
decisions.reason: The tribes on Gerizim stand for the blessing, but this chapter gives only the curses (verses 15-26). The blessings for obedience are set out in 28:3-6. Joshua 8:33-34 tells how the law was read, with its blessing and curse, before the two halves of the people.

decisions.choice: Mount Gerizim: the southern of the two mountains at Shechem
decisions.reason: Gerizim faces Ebal across the valley of Shechem (11:29). The blessing is set there, the curse on Ebal (verse 13).

decisions.choice: these tribes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "tribes" to say what "these" refers to.

records.source: וְאֵ֛לֶּה יַֽעַמְד֥וּ עַל־הַקְּלָלָ֖ה בְּהַ֣ר עֵיבָ֑ל רְאוּבֵן֙ גָּ֣ד וְאָשֵׁ֔ר וּזְבוּלֻ֖ן דָּ֥ן וְנַפְתָּלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And these will stand for the curse on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad and Asher and Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.
pieces: And these tribes are to stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.

L.13: And these shall stand for the curse on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad and Asher and Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.

R.13: These tribes must stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.

decisions.choice: the six tribes on Ebal: the sons of the servant women, with Reuben and Zebulun
decisions.reason: Gad and Asher are sons of Zilpah, Dan and Naphtali sons of Bilhah, the servant women given to Leah and Rachel. Reuben is Leah's firstborn, who lost his place by lying with his father's wife (Genesis 35:22; 49:3-4; compare verse 20), and Zebulun her youngest son (Genesis 35:23-26).

decisions.choice: for the curse: standing over against the curse, not to curse the people
decisions.reason: Verse 12 says the first group stands "to bless the people". This verse does not say "to curse the people" but only "for the curse": they stand on the side of the mountain where the curse is spoken.

decisions.choice: these tribes
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

records.source: וְעָנ֣וּ הַלְוִיִּ֗ם וְאָֽמְר֛וּ אֶל־כָּל־אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל ק֥וֹל רָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And will answer the Levites and say to every man of Israel [with a] voice loud:
pieces: Then the Levites are to call out in a loud voice to {{gender:all the people|all the men}} of Israel:

L.14: And the Levites shall answer and say to {{gender:everyone|every man}} of Israel with a loud voice:

R.14: The Levites must shout to {{gender:all the people|all the men}} of Israel:

decisions.choice: answer and say: speak up, proclaim
decisions.reason: "Answer" here does not reply to a question; it means to raise one's voice and speak in a solemn setting (21:7; 26:5).

decisions.choice: the Levites: probably the Levitical priests who carried the ark
alternatives: the whole tribe of Levi, standing apart from the twelve
decisions.reason: Levi is one of the tribes standing on Gerizim (verse 12), so "the Levites" who speak here are likely the priests of that tribe. In Joshua 8:33 the Levitical priests stand with the ark between the two halves of the people. The text does not explain how the two fit together.

decisions.choice: every man of Israel: the whole people, men and women
decisions.reason: The phrase names the whole people, all of whom answer "Amen" (verse 15). Joshua 8:35 says that women, children and foreigners were present when the law was read.

decisions.choice: call out in a loud voice (Balanced); shout (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable render "answer and say with a loud voice" by a single verb of loud speaking, following meaning decision m1.

records.source: אָר֣וּר הָאִ֡ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַעֲשֶׂה֩ פֶ֨סֶל וּמַסֵּכָ֜ה תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה מַעֲשֵׂ֛ה יְדֵ֥י חָרָ֖שׁ וְשָׂ֣ם בַּסָּ֑תֶר וְעָנ֧וּ כָל־הָעָ֛ם וְאָמְר֖וּ אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is] the man who makes [a] carved image or [a] cast image, [an] abomination of Yahweh, [the] work of [the] hands of [a] craftsman, and sets [it] in the secret place; and will answer all the people and say, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who makes a carved or cast idol, a thing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} detests, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets it up in secret.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.15: 'Cursed [is] the {{gender:one|man}} who makes a carved image or a cast image, an abomination to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the work of the hands of a craftsman, and sets [it] up in secret.' And all the people shall answer and say, 'Amen.'

R.15: 'Cursed is anyone who makes an idol, carved or made of melted metal, and sets it up in secret. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} hates such things made by a craftsman.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: cursed: placed under God's curse
decisions.reason: To be "cursed" is to be handed over to harm and loss from God, cut off from the blessing of the covenant (28:15-19; Genesis 3:14; 4:11). The words are a solemn statement made before God, not a wish for human revenge, and the punishment is left to him.

decisions.choice: Amen: surely, so let it be
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning firm or sure. Said in answer to a curse or an oath, it agrees to it and accepts it as binding on oneself: the people declare that if they do these things, the curse may fall on them (Numbers 5:22; Nehemiah 5:13; Jeremiah 11:5). The word itself passed into the worship of later Israel and of the church (1 Chronicles 16:36; 1 Corinthians 14:16).

decisions.choice: in secret: wrongs hidden from human eyes
decisions.reason: Several of the twelve curses name acts done where no witness sees: idols set up in secret, a neighbor struck down in secret (verse 24), wrongs inside the household. A human court needs two or three witnesses (17:6; 19:15); what it cannot see, the curse hands over to God, who sees.

decisions.choice: a carved image or a cast image: an idol of wood or stone, or one of molten metal
decisions.reason: The first word names an image cut from wood or stone, the second one made by pouring melted metal into a mold, like the golden calf (Exodus 32:4; Deuteronomy 9:12). Together they cover every kind of idol, the very thing forbidden by the second commandment (5:8). "Abomination to the LORD" is what he finds detestable (7:25-26).

decisions.choice: the man who: anyone who
decisions.reason: The word is "man", but the curse is on anyone who does this; the people who answer are the whole nation.

decisions.choice: the same response formula in all twelve curses
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew says the people "answer and say"; in verses 16-26 it says only "say". Literal keeps the difference. Balanced and Readable use one wording for the response in all twelve curses, so the repeated pattern is heard, and keep "Amen" at every level.

decisions.choice: splits off the description of the idol into its own sentence
decisions.reason: Readable gives the curse first, then says in a short second sentence that the LORD hates such man-made things.

records.source: אָר֕וּר מַקְלֶ֥ה אָבִ֖יו וְאִמּ֑וֹ וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] dishonoring his father or his mother; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who dishonors {{gender:their|his}} father or mother.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.16: 'Cursed [is the one who] dishonors {{gender:their|his}} father or {{gender:their|his}} mother.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.16: 'Cursed is anyone who treats {{gender:their|his}} father or mother with scorn.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: dishonors: treats as of little worth, with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to make light of someone. It is the opposite of "honor" in the fifth commandment (5:16), and covers both scornful words and neglect (Exodus 21:17; Leviticus 20:9).

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

records.source: אָר֕וּר מַסִּ֖יג גְּב֣וּל רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] moving [the] boundary of his neighbor; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who moves {{gender:their|his}} neighbor's boundary marker.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.17: 'Cursed [is the one who] moves {{gender:their|his}} neighbor's boundary [marker].' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.17: 'Cursed is anyone who moves the stone that marks the edge of {{gender:their|his}} neighbor's land.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: moving a boundary marker: secretly taking a neighbor's land
decisions.reason: Fields were marked off by stones. Moving one quietly stole land, and with it the family's living and inheritance, the share given by God (19:14; Proverbs 22:28; 23:10).

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

decisions.choice: boundary marker (Literal, Balanced); the stone that marks the edge of ... land (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means "boundary"; what can be moved is the stone that marks it. Literal brackets "marker"; Readable explains it.

records.source: אָר֕וּר מַשְׁגֶּ֥ה עִוֵּ֖ר בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] making wander [a] blind [person] on the road; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person astray on the road.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.18: 'Cursed [is the one who] makes a blind [person] wander on the road.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.18: 'Cursed is anyone who makes a blind person lose the way.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: misleading the blind: cruelty to someone who cannot defend himself
decisions.reason: Leviticus 19:14 forbids putting a stumbling block before the blind. Leading a blind person off the road is a wrong he cannot see or name, and so it is left to God.

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

records.source: אָר֗וּר מַטֶּ֛ה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט גֵּר־יָת֖וֹם וְאַלְמָנָ֑ה וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] turning aside [the] justice of [the] sojourner, fatherless, and widow; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who denies justice to the outsider, the fatherless, or the widow.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.19: 'Cursed [is the one who] turns aside the justice due the sojourner, the fatherless, or the widow.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.19: 'Cursed is anyone who keeps outsiders, orphans or widows from being treated fairly.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: turning aside justice: twisting a case against those who have no defender
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 24:17 and 16:19. God himself sees that these people get justice (10:18), and he commands Israel to do the same.

decisions.choice: the sojourner, the fatherless, the widow: people without land or a man to stand for them
decisions.reason: A sojourner was a foreigner living in Israel without a family share of land. The fatherless and the widow had lost the man who would speak for them in court. All three could easily be wronged.

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

decisions.choice: outsider (Balanced, Readable); orphans (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "outsider" for the sojourner; Readable says "orphans" for children who have lost their father.

records.source: אָר֗וּר שֹׁכֵב֙ עִם־אֵ֣שֶׁת אָבִ֔יו כִּ֥י גִלָּ֖ה כְּנַ֣ף אָבִ֑יו וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] lying with [the] wife of his father, for he has uncovered [the] skirt of his father; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his father's wife, for he has violated his father's marriage.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.20: 'Cursed [is the one who] lies with his father's wife, for he has uncovered his father's skirt.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.20: 'Cursed is anyone who has sex with his father's wife, because he has brought shame on his father.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: his father's wife: any wife of his father, not only his own mother
decisions.reason: A man could have more than one wife, so his father's wife could be his stepmother. The law forbids such a union in Leviticus 18:8 and 20:11; Reuben's act with Bilhah is remembered against him (Genesis 35:22; 49:4).

decisions.choice: uncovered his father's skirt: violated what belongs to his father as husband
decisions.reason: The "skirt" or corner of a man's garment, spread over a woman, stood for taking her as wife (Ruth 3:9; Ezekiel 16:8). To uncover it is to dishonor the father's marriage. The same words are in 23:1 (Hebrew numbering).

decisions.choice: lies with: has sexual relations with
decisions.reason: The verb "lie" with "with" is the usual polite way of speaking of sexual union, as in verses 21-23.

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

decisions.choice: has sexual relations with; violated his father's marriage (Balanced); brought shame on his father (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the idioms mean, following meaning decisions m2 and m3. Literal keeps "lies with" and "uncovered his father's skirt".

records.source: אָר֕וּר שֹׁכֵ֖ב עִם־כָּל־בְּהֵמָ֑ה וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] lying with any animal; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with any animal.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.21: 'Cursed [is the one who] lies with any animal.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.21: 'Cursed is anyone who has sex with an animal.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: lying with an animal: forbidden to men and women alike
decisions.reason: Leviticus 18:23 and 20:15-16 forbid this to both men and women, and Exodus 22:18 (Hebrew numbering) sets the death penalty for it. "Lies with" is as in verse 20.

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

records.source: אָר֗וּר שֹׁכֵב֙ עִם־אֲחֹת֔וֹ בַּת־אָבִ֖יו א֣וֹ בַת־אִמּ֑וֹ וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] lying with his sister, [the] daughter of his father or [the] daughter of his mother; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his sister, whether she is his father's daughter or his mother's daughter.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.22: 'Cursed [is the one who] lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.22: 'Cursed is anyone who has sex with his sister, even if they have only the same father or only the same mother.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: his sister, daughter of his father or of his mother: a full sister or a half-sister
decisions.reason: With more than one wife in a household, a man could have sisters who shared only his father or only his mother. The law covers both (Leviticus 18:9, 11; 20:17). Compare Abraham and Sarah before the law (Genesis 20:12) and the wrong done to Tamar (2 Samuel 13).

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

decisions.choice: even if they have only the same father or only the same mother
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the curse covers a half-sister as well as a full sister.

records.source: אָר֕וּר שֹׁכֵ֖ב עִם־חֹֽתַנְתּ֑וֹ וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] lying with his mother-in-law; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his mother-in-law.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.23: 'Cursed [is the one who] lies with his mother-in-law.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.23: 'Cursed is anyone who has sex with his wife's mother.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: his mother-in-law: his wife's mother
decisions.reason: The word is the mother of a man's wife. Leviticus 18:17 and 20:14 forbid a man to take both a woman and her mother.

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

records.source: אָר֕וּר מַכֵּ֥ה רֵעֵ֖הוּ בַּסָּ֑תֶר וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] striking his neighbor in the secret place; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who strikes down {{gender:their|his}} neighbor in secret.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.24: 'Cursed [is the one who] strikes {{gender:their|his}} neighbor in secret.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.24: 'Cursed is anyone who secretly attacks and kills {{gender:their|his}} neighbor.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: strikes: a deadly blow, murder done in secret
alternatives: attacks, whether or not the victim dies
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike, and is often used of a blow that kills (19:11; Exodus 21:12). Here it most likely means a secret murder, though it could also cover a hidden attack that wounds.

decisions.choice: in secret: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: A killing with no witnesses could not be tried in court (17:6). The curse puts it before God, who sees what is hidden.

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

decisions.choice: strikes down (Balanced); attacks and kills (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the blow is a deadly one, following meaning decision m1.

records.source: אָרוּר֙ לֹקֵ֣חַ שֹׁ֔חַד לְהַכּ֥וֹת נֶ֖פֶשׁ דָּ֣ם נָקִ֑י וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] taking [a] bribe to strike [a] person, blood innocent; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.25: 'Cursed [is the one who] takes a bribe to strike a person, innocent blood.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.25: 'Cursed is anyone who accepts money to kill an innocent person.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: to strike a person, innocent blood: to bring about the death of someone innocent
alternatives: a corrupt judge or false witness only
decisions.reason: "Innocent blood" stands beside "a person" to say who is killed: someone who has done nothing to deserve death (19:10; 21:8-9). The one who takes the bribe may be a hired killer, or a judge or witness paid to have an innocent person condemned (16:19; Exodus 23:7-8).

decisions.choice: a bribe: a gift that buys a decision
decisions.reason: The word is the gift paid to sway a judge or win someone over. Deuteronomy says God takes no bribe (10:17) and forbids judges to take one, for it blinds the eyes of the wise (16:19).

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

decisions.choice: to kill an innocent person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join "strike a person" and "innocent blood" into one plain phrase, following meaning decision m1.

records.source: אָר֗וּר אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹא־יָקִ֛ים אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַתּוֹרָֽה־הַזֹּ֖את לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אוֹתָ֑ם וְאָמַ֥ר כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אָמֵֽן׃פ
records.gloss: Cursed [is one] who not will establish [the] words of the law the this to do them; and will say all the people, amen.
pieces: 'Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

L.26: 'Cursed [is the one] who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them.' And all the people shall say, 'Amen.'

R.26: 'Cursed is anyone who does not stand by the words of this teaching and obey them.' Then all the people must say, 'Amen.'

decisions.choice: uphold: make the words stand, put them into effect
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something stand or keep it standing. One who does not keep the law's words in practice lets them fall. This last curse sums up the eleven before it: the curse rests on anyone who does not live by the whole law.

decisions.choice: the words of this law (no "all")
alternatives: all the words of this law
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "the words of this law". The Samaritan Pentateuch and the ancient Greek translation read "all the words of this law", and Paul quotes the verse in that form in Galatians 3:10. The sense is close either way, since the curse sums up the whole law.

decisions.choice: Cursed ... Amen: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The same formula as in verse 15: the Levites declare the curse, and the people accept it with "Amen".

decisions.choice: this teaching; stand by
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for "law", as in verses 3 and 8, and "stand by" for "uphold".
